name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes a Democratic win a steep climb
Rogers holds roughly a 40-to-1 fundraising advantage over McInnis
Prediction markets price the Democratic upset odds near 1%
No polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: An R+23 district, a well-funded incumbent, and prediction markets pricing Democratic odds at about 1% all point the same direction; even a national environment worth several points to Democrats leaves McInnis far short of the swing needed.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a national wave large enough to move a 20-point margin would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, and incumbent Mike Rogers enters the general election as a heavy favorite. The district's R+23 partisan lean gives any Democrat a steep climb, and Rogers is an established incumbent seeking another term. No public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive.

The money gap is stark: Rogers has raised about $2.45 million and holds $2.66 million on hand, while Democrat Lee McInnis has raised roughly $61,000 with under $10,000 available. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 1% chance of an upset. Even with a national environment that favors Democrats by several points, the combination of district lean, incumbency, and financial dominance points to a comfortable Republican hold. The absence of polling is the main source of uncertainty, leaving modest room for error.
